why: Protocol section 4's pairing rule, and X17's false-exclusion requirement: BOTH NUMBERS ARE REPORTED OR NEITHER IS. The negative suite alone cannot tell a control that refuses the seventeen adverse cases from one that refuses everything, and a control that refuses everything passes every adverse row. Each fixture here is the registry edit its paired adverse case's BENIGN column implies, and it must PASS validation. A benign fixture that fails is a false exclusion, which is a defect of the same class as a missed adverse case and is reported the same way.
checked_by: tools/run_positive_fixtures.py: declared-but-absent and present-but-undeclared both fail, and a fixture that does NOT pass validation fails
validate_contracts.py: the positive run's own count must equal this one, every declared fixture must have passed, and the declared count must not fall below the floor
floor_why: A literal, for the reason every other floor in this package is a literal: a count derived from the directory it measures is satisfied by the empty directory. Seventeen is one benign case per adverse case of selection-record section 12.5, and dropping one would drop the pairing rule for that row. Lowering this number is a decision and should read like one. RAISED BY R18 (the Step 6 repair of the F2 layer): negative 56 -> 91, positive 17 -> 52. Thirty-five new adverse cases and thirty-five paired benign ones, one per finding the four Step 6 reviews raised against the contracts, plus one pair per guard that had none. F6C-16 measured 14 of 30 guards exercised by a paired fixture; every registered guard has one now, and the count is derived rather than quoted -- `comm -12 <(grep -rhoE 'guard\.[a-z0-9_.]+' fixtures/negative | sort -u) <(grep -rhoE 'guard\.[a-z0-9_.]+' fixtures/positive | sort -u) | wc -l`. Lowering either number is still two edits and a written reason. RAISED TO THE COMMITTED COUNT BY THE RC5 REPAIR: positive 53 -> 55 (RC5-01, RC5-03: the allowlist-literal pair and the not-admitted pair) and 55 -> 56 (RC5-02: the pin-coverage pair). R20 (F6A-10): 56 -> 57, the closed-enum membership pair.
